candidate.explanation: v17 post-audit-closure candidate, cut 2026-08-11 on branch v17, built directly on the prior v16 candidate (which closed the authenticated-E2E blocker). v17 executes the Post-Audit Closure pack (LB-V17-01..07, XAPP-V17-01): (01) the trial paywall now models eligibility as an explicit finite state (loading|eligible|ineligible|unavailable) so a failed billing read can never show a false 3-day-trial promise; (02) exact Stripe ownership on every webhook object — subscriptions self-identify by metadata.source='launchbloom', a bare app_user_id key is no longer proof, a foreign stamp fails closed, charge/dispute ownership requires an exact stamp or an owned-customer parent (a narrow, measured legacy price fallback remains); (03) a versioned, TTL'd, user/workspace-scoped browser draft registry replaces indefinite full-content localStorage, with logout/delete purge and a Clear-drafts control; (04) README + rendered LAUNCH_STATE de-staled; (05) a sanitized production-readiness evidence schema+validator (readiness:validate) mirroring the live-money rehearsal validator; (07) a predeclared value-cohort plan over the existing scorecard. Because v17 changed frontend source and the served bundle (now index-DVEF1GCL) plus backend billing/webhook logic, the prior candidate's checks were RE-RUN at this exact commit 64e7691 on 2026-08-11 — lint 0/0, 932 unit tests, build, fresh bundle index-DVEF1GCL, public browser journeys 52 pass, and the authenticated matrix RE-RUN 45/45 green against a disposable non-production Supabase (SHA-pinned to 64e76914 in test-results/e2e-auth-evidence.json), export 15/15, router reachability 15/15, hero contrast, launch integrity. CARRY-FORWARD (valid by this manifest's own standard): `git diff b234dad..64e7691` over backend/migrations/ and over backend/lib/launch-config.js + backend/scripts/release-check.js is EMPTY, so the applied migration set and the production config-gate are byte-identical to the prior candidate; the migrations-applied and production-readiness observations carry forward, with the standing owner action to re-confirm GET /api/admin/readiness against the deployed 64e7691 before opening (now with the readiness:validate evidence gate from LB-V17-05). Documentation-only commits after this SHA (including this launch-state record) do not invalidate the candidate; anything under backend/, app-src/, app/, e2e/, api/ or config does.

blockers.title: react-router / react-router-dom 7.18.2 carry an open high advisory GHSA-qwww-vcr4-c8h2 (RSC-mode CSRF bypass)
blockers.closure: GHSA-qwww-vcr4-c8h2 is fixed only in react-router 8.3.0, which removes the react-router-dom package and requires React 19 / Vite 7 / Node >=22.22 — a stack upgrade beyond v14's scope. `npm audit --omit=dev` reports 2 high at 81993ff. NOT reachable in practice: the advisory states it only affects applications using the unstable RSC APIs, and this app ships no RSC or SSR entry point (declarative BrowserRouter only). ACCEPTED for public_paid on 2026-08-04 with the rationale below; it keeps its real status (the advisory is NOT closed) and is revisited at the react-router 8 / React 19 / Vite 7 migration or sooner if a 7.x backport ships. Introduced alongside SC-P0-06 (ca3eaa8), which closed the three previously-open 6.30.4 advisories.

accepted_risk.revisit_at: react-router 8 / React 19 / Vite 7 migration, or sooner if a 7.x backport of GHSA-qwww-vcr4-c8h2 ships
accepted_risk.reachability_guard: npm run check:router (backend/lib/router-reachability.js): fails if any RSC/SSR/server-router indicator appears, so the 'not reachable' basis is mechanically enforced, not asserted.
resolution_paths: A: a safe patched 7.x release of react-router-dom that fixes GHSA-qwww-vcr4-c8h2 without the 8.x break — adopt it and close this blocker.
B: a separately scoped react-router 8 / React 19 / Vite 7 migration with its own regression plan (breaking; removes react-router-dom).
accepted_risk.dependency_watch: Watch react-router advisories and the react-router-dom 7.x line; re-run `npm run audit` before every candidate cut and reassess if a 7.x fix or a reachable RSC/SSR entry point is ever introduced.
accepted_risk.rationale: The advisory affects ONLY applications using the unstable React Server Components APIs. This app ships none: all app-src router imports are 'react-router-dom', it mounts a single declarative <BrowserRouter>, there is no RSC/SSR entry point, and the build is a pure client SPA (proof in reachability_evidence). how_to_create_a_new_candidate: 1. Land all intended work on the release branch. No feature work after this point.
2. Set candidate.sha to the exact frozen commit and candidate.state to "frozen".

3. Re-run every required check at that SHA and record status, observed_at_sha and an evidence reference for each. A check whose underlying code changed since the last candidate may NOT be carried forward — re-run it or mark it not_run.
4. Attach owner evidence references for the live items.
5. Run `npm run launch:gate`. It recomputes both verdicts; it cannot be argued with.
6. Run `npm run launch:render` to regenerate docs/LAUNCH_STATE.md.

Any commit after step 2 that changes code creates a NEW candidate: the SHA no longer matches HEAD, every check pinned to the old SHA stops counting, and the verdict returns to NO-GO. Documentation-only commits (docs/ and the prompt packs) do not.
